actionability.justification: The rule gives a concrete behavioral trigger (ask before deleting/overwriting anything, including self-created test/scratch artifacts, when it could conflict with an earlier stated constraint), which is specific enough to change behavior, though "could plausibly conflict" leaves some judgment call to the agent.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It generalizes past the single deletion event to cover the underlying failure mode (treating self-labeled 'fake'/scratch content as exempt from earlier constraints) without collapsing into a vague platitude like "be careful with destructive actions."

leakage.justification: The remedy text uses only generic nouns (files/content, test/scratch/'fake' artifacts) and never names the specific project, migration, or incident details.

routing_fitness.justification: claude-md is a reasonable low-cost vehicle for a judgment-based rule (a hook can't evaluate 'conflicts with an earlier instruction'), but the target global CLAUDE.md already contains an extensive 'Executing actions with care' section instructing confirmation before destructive/irreversible actions, so this is largely additive nuance rather than filling a clear gap, and elevating a singleton incident straight to permanent global scope is a somewhat heavier remedy than the evidence strictly warrants.

trigger_quality.justification: This is routed as a claude-md rule rather than a skill, so there is no explicit "Use when ..." trigger to evaluate; the rule is always-loaded and its firing condition (potential conflict with an earlier constraint) is embedded in prose rather than a crisp, checkable trigger.
